verdicts.evidence: src/TreeHash.jl:47 now reads `_nonempty(path, skip) || continue  # git tracks no empty directory`, replacing the always-false `isempty(_nonempty(path, skip)) && continue`. `_nonempty` (src/TreeHash.jl:66-71) returns true only when the subtree holds >=1 file, so `|| continue` correctly skips a recursively-empty directory instead of pushing a 40000 entry for it. test/treehash.jl (new) asserts `G.TreeHash.tree_hash(dir) == git('write-tree')` over a real git repo containing a nested empty subdirectory, and separately asserts a tree holding only an empty subdirectory hashes to git's canonical empty-tree id 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 — both pass only with the corrected guard (I re-derived the logic and git's own semantics independently).

class_surfaces.evidence: guard inverted to `_nonempty(path, skip) || continue`, matches the hint exactly, verified against real `git write-tree`
text 'empty directories omitted' left unchanged, and is now true given the code fix; no edit needed here since the docstring was already the correct claim, only the code was wrong

grepped every `isempty(` call in src/ and ext/: every other call site applies isempty to a real collection (array, string, dict, etc.), not a Bool-returning predicate; TreeHash.jl:47 was the only instance of this bug class

Both docstrings (WitnessResult at :33, run_one at :147-148) were reworded from 'was never seen to fail'/'errored' to 'errored and failed nothing' / 'failed nothing ... one that also failed is :broken', which is now an accurate description of the code. test/witnesses.jl adds `blocked_but_failed.jl` (one true failing @test plus one erroring @test under a `# blocked:` header) and asserts its status is `:broken` (not `:blocked`) and its reason contains '1 assertion(s) failed' — I traced the branch by hand and confirmed f=1,e=1 takes the new `:broken` path.
